text:
maria: Heads-up — SparrowHawk customer LoRA adapter landed in `adapters/sparrowhawk-lora` and I ran the int4-onboard smoke. Getting KV cache segfault inside runtime for sequence lengths >1024. Error snippet: ```runtime error: kv-cache out-of-bounds at kv.c:421
stack: ...``` Anyone seen this pattern? Need a minimal quick-eval pack (10 prompts: invoices, support Qs, long-context) to reproduce and a perf baseline vs fp16.
alex: Can you paste the command you used? which model checkpoint + quant recipe?
maria: `python tools/run_smoke.py --model ./models/gpt-gigantica-8b --adapter adapters/sparrowhawk-lora --quant int4 --seq_len 2048 --batch 1` Got crash within first forward. Used recipe `int4-fastmix-v2`.
sam_q: :eyes: sounds like a KV stride mismatch introduced by the adapter's prompt token remap. Try `--kv-policy compatibility` or run with `RUNTIME_DEBUG=1` and dump kv shapes. Also please attach quick eval pack — I'll run locally.
jen_cs: SparrowHawk's SLA is 250ms p95 T2 for chat flows. They will hit this on Dedicated if quant fails. I'll ping the customer for sample dialogs.
maria: Uploaded a quick-eval zip to our internal bucket: https://s3.redwood-internal/evals/sparrowhawk_quick_eval_v1.zip — includes 12 prompts and expected outputs.
ops-qa: I ran the eval on dedicated-nightly with `int4-fastmix-v2` + adapter. Repro: same segfault after ~4 tokens. Log: `segfault at 0x0` pointing to `kv_map_get`. Attaching stack trace.
sam_q: Ok that's consistent. Two action items: 1) try `--quant int4-safe` (slower kernels) to see if kernel selection mitigates; 2) run adapter-only forward with `--keep-kv=false` to isolate. I'll pick this up after lunch.
maria: noted — flagging for eng-runtime. @chris_rt can you triage the kernel selection fallback? (cc @sam_q)
chris_rt: I'll take a look. Can you drop the crash core and the adapter weight diff (we need to check tensor dtype/name mismatches)?
jen_cs: customer contact confirmed sample dialogs, will send credentials for private bucket.
maria: thanks all. I'll post a tiny reproduction gist and update this thread. :thumbsup:
